title_en: Technology and Engineering (9/20): Designing a New Chip
note_en: 为了 (wèile) "in order to" introduces a purpose, and that clause normally comes first: 为了提高运算速度，他们反复调整电路的布局 "To increase computing speed, they adjusted the circuit layout again and again." English often puts the purpose at the end ("they adjusted it to increase speed"); in Chinese, putting 为了… after the main clause sounds marked and is usually rephrased with 是为了.
